Some games include a few features you're looking for, and others cover most of them. What's on your checklist for the perfect co-op game?
What's on your checklist for a great co-op game?

Some of the things I appreciate in a good co-op game:

  • co-op campaign, since I enjoy playing through a story with friends
  • 4-player co-op or more, since you really get a group dynamic going with more than two players as an option.
  • a good teamwork emphasis, because I want to have to rely on my buddies to survive and progress through the game
  • co-op that's integrated into the experience and not just tacked on top of a singleplayer dynamic

I enjoy a few different genres of games, but these are the core features that I look for in a good co-op game.

Personally:

A game with good netcode, if I want to play online I want the game to have very little lag between the two players. (Also no drop outs, and if drop outs do happen, the ability for your partner to rejoin without losing progress.)

A game which is simple to pick up and play, as I might be cooping with someone who is less skilled at games and I don't want to massively out-perform them just because I play games more than them. I want my partner to be just as useful as I am.

Multiple controller methods, so I can play whilst in bed with a controller, or play on my chair with keyboard and mouse, or I can play with keyboard and mouse but my coop partner can use a controller.

A game which has complimenting skills that scale to how many players are in the party. Often I play with only 1 other person, and a lot of skills are balanced around having 4 people in a team, not 2 people in a team, making skills which "Provides extra damage to each ally" weaker because it's only giving that number to 2 people. Games which scale the bonus of the skill for the amount of players in the team are the best (I have seen games do this, although I cannot remember which games exactly.)

A game which has a good pace, but does not require you to much as fast as possible to complete. Often me and my coop partner play at different speeds, and it can be frustrating to either wait for your partner all the time, or always be left behind.

Instanced drops, so you are not stealing loot off of teammates, everyone has their own, seperate drops (Such as Torchlight 2, Borderlands etc). However the ability to trade or drop those items for the team is important too.

The ability to disable voice chat in game (As skype/teamspeak/ventrillo is often used, not the ingame chat)

I prefer shared exp, so neither player is higher leveled than the other players (Goes back to my earlier point of all teammates being equally useful).

I also like a game that rewards good communication, it feels awesome when you're winning because you're talking to each other and cooperating and planning together to take on a challenge you couldn't handle alone.

Games that increase challenge for coop in unique and interesting ways, not simply increasing the health of enemies and making them bullet-sponges.

I also like having the ability to grief your teammates (Magicka style) although the option to turn off friendly fire can be good too :)

It sounds like much of what you're looking for is balance. Balance in how the game handles different amounts of players, different skill levels, and pacing of the gameplay itself. I think that's a good core feature that when done well makes for a smooth co-op experience. I also agree that netcode is a good priority. It amazes me how games with small populations like Titanfall sometimes have faster matchmaking than games with large populations like Call of Duty. Netcode is even more important in co-op because desynchronizing can affect where a target appears compared to its actual location. I see this happen in Halo 4 and in Payday 2 occasionally.
I didn't even think of drop-in and drop-out support, but that's always great to have.

I think you've got a good list here. I especially like what you said about communication. I think games that encourage good communication tend to encourage good teamwork as well. Good list!

I've played a lot of coop games and these are the things I've noticed.

Also having a a broad range of enjoyable traits is good. For example I love divinity original sin for the tactical combat, my coop partner loves it for the story line and fantastical world. (And talking to animals.)

That's a good point. It's probably difficult to do, but I love when a game is able to juggle different elements effectively. Diablo 3 for example, which I enjoy for the gameplay and my friend enjoys for the storyline.

I agree. Another note on balance, I loved Guild Wars 2, I was able to play with my coop partner even though they had spent so much less time on the game than I had. The way that game balanced lower leveled events and areas for higher leveled characters was really good.

That's a great feature. Diablo 3 does this, but Borderlands 2 does not. I always have to coordinate with my buddies in Borderlands 2 to find similar level characters, or just bite the bullet and start over for the umpteenth time. Payday 2 also doesn't scale levels, but it's less of an issue because the game isn't story based. I think for story based RPGs it's a powerful feature to have.
If it's a console exclusive, have split screen support! If my roommate and I want to play a game together, we shouldn't both have to spend $400+ to play it together.

I'm definitely with you there! Halo 5's lack of splitscreen has me considering saving up for a Wii U. I hadn't thought of it before, but Nintendo does have a great library of couch co-op games that would compliment the handful that I have on my Xbox One. It's sad to see it disappearing from the Xbox/Playstation camps, but there are still holdouts here and there.

The same console co-op is the primary selling point of the WiiU for me. I've seen deals on PS4's that come with 4 controllers and I just can't fathom why someone would buy 4 PS4 controllers. I can't count the number of Wii controllers and accessories I still have.

I generally play ps3 co-op with my wife and/or kids.

  • Configurable friendly fire, friendly fire will cause too many fights amongst the kids if it is on, but it's a nice challenge when the wife and I are playing.

  • Co-op campaign, I'm only going to play the game once and it will be co-op so I need to be able to get the whole experience.

  • Designed for couch co-op, recently games are being designed for online co-op at the expense of couch co-op (I'm looking at your Dragon's Crown). I need to be able to progress my characters at the same rate regardless of who is player 1 and who is player 2.

  • Everyone needs to get their own drops, my wife is a loot fiend who will lie, cheat, and steal to get my loot (I have to take my controller when I get a snack).

Two of these are points I didn't think of. I appreciate when friendly fire is configurable because it's really a personal preference thing. And I'm with you on the loot drops, since there's always one in the group who grabs more quickly than the rest :p

• APJ Abdul Kalam speaks to M.J. Akbar about presidential elections 2012

Q. In the book, you mention that you do the morning namaaz.

A. Yes, every day, whenever possible. My father was very strict about namaaz and would wake me up at 4 a.m. and take me to the mosque. I also fast.

Q. So why is it that the so-called Muslim leaders in the North always have the feeling that you are not a practising Muslim?

A. First of all, I am an Indian and try to be a good human being. People can call me XYZ, that's their freedom of expression. There is no conflict of any kind regarding my faith in Islam. I often visit temples and churches as well. God is everywhere.

Q. You had several conversations with Vajpayee when he was PM. In your own assessment, do you consider Modi guilty of the Gujarat riots?

A. I'm not there to pronounce a judgment on the Gujarat riots; that's the work of the judiciary. But I will narrate another incident about Vajpayee. When he took over the Cabinet, I was scientific adviser. He called me to his office one night and offered me a Cabinet post. I was busy with the Agni and nuclear programme. The next morning I went back to meet him. He sat in his room, surrounded by trays of sweets, which were a weakness of his. I told him I was sorry but I couldn't become a minister as my work on the two programmes would suffer. Later, I finished work on the programmes, left the government and went back to teaching. It was then that Vajpayee called me and asked me to become president.

Q. Do you think Vajpayee considered Modi guilty of the riots?

A. I can't speak for him. Whether the riots were planned or just happened, we don't know but any right-thinking individual would not support any wrong being done to a community. When I visited Gujarat, I did not go to investigate what happened and whether Modi was right or wrong, but to remove the pain and accelerate relief work.
